marks.gloss_en: מאי קסברי רבנן?... אלא לאו שמע מינה -- only on אי אפשר לצמצם does one heifer in partnership, with a stipulation, make sense
rather, conclude from it: the Rabbis hold it is impossible to be exact, even by the hand of man
found exactly between two towns -- they would not break [a heifer's neck]
rather, all agree it is possible to be exact, and here they dispute over 'the nearest' and not [two] nearest
and the Sages say: they bring one heifer in partnership and stipulate
ומי מצית אמרת הכי? והתני סיפא: שהיה רבי יוסי אומר כל שחליפיו ביד כהן פטור מן המתנות ... חליפין ביד כהן -- אין, אין חליפין ביד כהן -- לא! (18a.15-18b.1)
Rava: they made one who does not acquire like one who acquires -- though it did not reach his hand, it is as if it reached his hand and he sold it to the Israelite in its blemish
R' Elazar: all concede regarding an uncertain firstborn whose replacement is not in the priest's hand, that it is obligated in the gifts
what you might have said: R' Yosei's reason is that if you obligate him in the gifts he will come to shearing and labor -- [so he exempts] even without a replacement in the priest's hand
and the second [lamb] grazes until it becomes blemished
תרגמנא מסיפא -- the reading is drawn from R' Akiva's latter clause, המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה
והא אנן משמנין ביניהן תנן! -- but we learned 'they assess between them'
עד דאכלת כפניתא בבבל, תרגמנא מסיפא -- while you were eating dates in Babylonia, we explained it from the latter clause
R' Yochanan: the kohen takes the lean one
אמר ליה רבי חייא בר אבא לרבי יוחנן: והא אנן ״משמנין ביניהן״ תנן
תרגימנא מסיפא -- R' Akiva's seifa ruling (the claimant must bring proof) shows he does not divide, so the priest takes the lean one
עד דאכלת כפניתא בבבל תרגימנא מסיפא (18a.8) -- דקתני סיפא ... אלא מאי משמנין? שומן יהא ביניהן (18a.9)
if one of them died, R' Tarfon says: they divide
מאי טעמא דרבי טרפון? קא סבר ההוא דבריא נפק ברישא -- the better one is presumed the firstborn
he holds: the healthy one emerges first
